Introduction

Non-Ahmadi Muslims have only one single vague verse in the entire Quran to claim that Prophet Isa (AS) is alive in heaven: Quran 4:158.

They cling to one single word: Rafa.

They claim this word proves Isa (AS) flew up into the clouds and is sitting alive in outer space. But Rafa does not mean to fly to the skies, and it does not mean to stay alive.

Here is the universal rule:

Rafa is an Arabic verb that means to raise or elevate. When Allah raises (Rafa’a) humans, He only raises their souls. Never their bodies.

Look at what the verse actually says:

بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا

“Nay, Allah raised him to Himself; and Allah is Mighty, Wise.”

[Quran 4:158]

Ask them a simple question: How does being raised to Allah mean being alive in the sky?

The verse says Allah raised him “to Himself” (Ilayh). Where does the Quran mention flying? Where does it mention the sky? Where does it say he stayed alive for thousands of years?

They have zero proof. They insert their own physical assumptions into the text.

First Challenge: The Linguistic Rule

First of all, show even one instance in the Arabic language, the Holy Quran, or the Hadith where Allah performs Rafa of a living human and it means raising their physical body.

You cannot show even once.

Whenever Allah raises a human being, it refers exclusively to raising their soul in spiritual status, honor, and closeness. It never means lifting flesh and bones into the clouds.

The burden of proof is completely on them. If they cannot produce a single linguistic example from the Quran or Sunnah, their physical claim collapses.

Second Challenge: Where Is Allah? The Dilemma

If non-Ahmadis still claim that Isa (AS) was physically raised “to Allah,” then ask them: Where is Allah?

Every Muslim scholar falls into one of two theological camps regarding the nature and direction of Allah. In both camps, claiming that Jesus flew to God creates an impossible contradiction.

Camp 1: The Majority of Muslims (Ash’aris, Maturidis, and Traditional Sunnis)

The vast majority of Sunnis believe that Allah does not have a physical direction, body, or place.

So we ask them:
– If Allah has no physical direction or location, where was Isa (AS) raised to?
– Flying up into the sky is not flying to Allah!
– You cannot physically travel toward someone who has no physical location!

If Allah has no physical place, then a physical journey into the clouds can never bring a human physically closer to Allah. The moment you say Isa (AS) traveled physically “to Allah,” you contradict your own creed.

Camp 2: The Minority Group (Salafis)

The Salafi school takes a literalist approach. They claim that Allah is in an upward direction, physically above the Throne (Arsh).

If this is their belief, they face an equally devastating problem:
– If Isa (AS) literally flew up to God, he must be above the Throne where Allah is!
– Why do you claim he is in the second heaven?

During the Mi’raj (Night Journey), Prophet Muhammad ﷺ met Isa (AS) in the second heaven, far below the seventh heaven, and infinitely below the Throne of Allah.

If Allah raised Isa (AS) “to Himself,” why was he left in the second heaven below the seven heavens, far away from the Throne?

By their own logic, Isa (AS) never reached Allah. Their literalist interpretation contradicts their own Hadith narrative.

Conclusion

Both groups end up contradicting their own core beliefs about Allah:
– Traditional Sunnis destroy their own creed by giving Allah a physical direction in the sky.
– Salafis destroy their own argument by trapping Isa (AS) in the second heaven, far away from the Throne.

“Raised him to Himself” (Rafa) never meant physical flight.

The historical context explains the verse perfectly. The opponents of Jesus claimed they killed him on the cross. Under Jewish law, anyone hung on a tree dies an accursed death, rejected by God.

Allah directly destroyed this false claim in Quran 4:158. Allah announced that instead of dying an accursed death on the cross, Isa (AS) had his soul raised to Allah in spiritual status, honor, and closeness. His prophetic honor was completely vindicated.

Summary and Key Takeaways

• Only One Vague Verse: Non-Ahmadi Muslims rely entirely on Quran 4:158 and the single word Rafa to claim Isa (AS) is alive.

• The Golden Rule: When Allah raises (Rafa) a human, He only raises their soul and spiritual rank, never their physical body.

• No Sky in the Text: Quran 4:158 states Allah raised him “to Himself” (Ilayh), not “to the sky” (ila al-samaa).

• The Sunni Dilemma: Traditional Sunnis believe Allah has no physical location, so physical flight cannot bring anyone closer to God.

• The Salafi Dilemma: Salafis claim Allah is above the Throne, yet their own Hadiths place Isa (AS) in the second heaven.

• The True Meaning: Rafa refutes the curse of the cross by confirming the spiritual elevation and noble status of Isa (AS) near Allah.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Rafa mean physical ascension in Quran 4:158?

No. In the Arabic language, the Quran, and Hadith, when Allah performs Rafa on a human being, it always means spiritual elevation, status, and honor. It never means lifting a physical human body into the sky.

Does Quran 4:158 mention Isa (AS) going to the sky?

No. The verse explicitly states Bal Rafa’ahullahu Ilayh (“Allah raised him to Himself”). It never mentions the sky (al-samaa), clouds, or outer space.

If Allah has no physical direction, how could Isa (AS) fly to Him?

He could not. For traditional Sunnis (Ash’aris and Maturidis) who believe Allah exists without a place or physical direction, claiming a physical body flew toward Allah is an impossible theological contradiction.

Why do Salafis face a contradiction regarding the second heaven?

Salafis argue Allah is above the Throne (Arsh). Yet Hadith reports state Isa (AS) was seen in the second heaven during Mi’raj. If he was raised “to Allah,” leaving him in the second heaven far away from the Throne contradicts their claim of physical ascension to God.

Why did Allah use the word Rafa in Quran 4:158?

The opponents of Isa (AS) claimed he died an accursed death on the cross. Allah used Rafa to prove that Isa (AS) was saved from a cursed death and exalted in spiritual honor and closeness to Allah.

Introduction

Anti-Ahmadis say Quran 4:158 proves Isa (AS) is alive in the sky, because Allah “raised him to Himself.” This is a misconception. One of Allah’s names is Al-Rafi (الرافع), “The Raiser.” He has raised believers to Himself since the beginning of time. Raising a person does not mean that person is alive in the sky. Here is why.

بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ

“Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself.”

[Quran 4:158]

Al-Rafi Is One of the 99 Names of Allah

Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d. 505 AH) explains this name in Al-Maqsad al-Asna. Al-Rafi is the One who raises the believers and lowers the disbelievers.

الْخَافِضُ الرَّافِعُ: هُوَ الَّذِي يَخْفِضُ الْكُفَّارَ بِالشَّقَاوَةِ وَيَرْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالسَّعَادَةِ، وَيَرْفَعُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ بِالتَّقْرِيبِ إِلَيْهِ

“Al-Khafid, Ar-Rafi: The One Who Abases the Unbeliever and Exalts the Believer. He is the One who abases the unbelievers through misfortune and exalts the believers through blessedness. He exalts His elect by drawing them near to Him.“

[Al-Maqsad al-Asna fi Sharh Ma’ani Asma’ Allah al-Husna]

Ghazali says Allah raises His elect “by drawing them near to Him.” The raising is closeness to Allah.

Allah Raises Believers

The Quran says the same about every believer.

يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ

“Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those to whom knowledge is given, to high ranks.”

[Quran 58:11]

Nobody reads this verse to mean that every believer is flown into the sky alive. Allah raises believers by rank and by nearness to Him.

When Allah raises (Rafa’a) humans, He only raises their souls. Never their bodies.

Allah raised Isa (AS) in the same way. He raises every believer. There is nothing unusual in it, and it does not tell us that the person is alive.

For the full proof, read Quran 4:157-158: The True Meaning of Rafa and What Does Rafa Mean in Islam?.

Conclusion

Al-Rafi is one of the names of Allah. He raises the believers and lowers the disbelievers, as Imam Ghazali writes in Al-Maqsad al-Asna. Quran 4:158 describes the same raising that every believer receives. It is not evidence that Isa (AS) is alive in the sky.

اِذۡ قَالَ اللّٰہُ یٰعِیۡسٰۤی اِنِّیۡ مُتَوَفِّیۡکَ وَ رَافِعُکَ اِلَیَّ وَ مُطَہِّرُکَ مِنَ الَّذِیۡنَ کَفَرُوۡا وَ جَاعِلُ الَّذِیۡنَ اتَّبَعُوۡکَ فَوۡقَ الَّذِیۡنَ کَفَرُوۡۤا اِلٰی یَوۡمِ الۡقِیٰمَۃِ ۚ ثُمَّ اِلَیَّ مَرۡجِعُکُمۡ فَاَحۡکُمُ بَیۡنَکُمۡ فِیۡمَا کُنۡتُمۡ فِیۡہِ تَخۡتَلِفُوۡنَ

When Allah said, ‘O Jesus, I will cause thee to die a natural death and will exalt thee to Myself, and will clear thee from the charges of those who disbelieve, and will place those who follow thee above those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me shall be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ.

[Quran 3:55]

Context

This verse very clearly and specifically talks about the natural death of Isa (A.S) and his spiritual exaltation towards Allah. Allah destroys the evil plans of the Jews, as mentioned in the previous verse “And they planned, and Allah also planned; and Allah is the Best of planners” (3:54). This plan of Jews is also recorded in 4:158, which was to crucify Isa (A.S) and humiliate him.

Crucifixion in their eyes meant that Isa (AS) would be accursed and proven a liar if he dies on the cross as per Deuteronomy 21:23. Hence Allah reveals that he will be the one to take his life (natural death), and the Jews will not be able to prove that he is accursed; instead, Allah will do the opposite i.e his Rafa unto Himself (spiritual exaltation).

Meaning of Tawaffa

Allah clearly says “اِنِّیۡ مُتَوَفِّیۡکَ” meaning “I will cause thee to die a natural death.” It cannot mean anything else in this context. Tawaffa (توفى) is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah does Tawaffi of a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul. This can be at the time of death, or sleep if night is mentioned. There is no other meaning for it.

• Tawaffa is used 25 times in the Quran. It means “Taking of the soul” every single time. Check here.

• Tawaffa is used many times in ahadith. It means “Taking of the soul” every single time. Check here.

• Muhammad (S.A.W) and Ali (R.A) translate Tawaffa as “death”. Check here.

• Arabic lexicons say that it means “Taking of the soul”. Check here.

• Non-Ahmadi (Sunni and Shias) agree that it means “Taking of the soul”. Check here.

• The challenge of the Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (A.S) to show an example that says “Take me”. Check here.

We just showed the general meaning of the word Tawaffa. No one can deny that it means anything but taking of the soul. In Surah Az-Zumar, Allah explains that there are only two ways He does the Tawaffa of humans. The first is at the time of their death and the second is at the time of sleep. There is no other meaning.

Allah takes away the souls of human beings at the time of their death; and of those also that are not yet dead, during their sleep. And then He retains those against which He has decreed death, and sends back the others till an appointed term. In that surely are Signs for a people who reflect.

[Quran 39:42]

Translation of Ibn Abbas (RA)

The greatest Mufassir of the Holy Quran specifically does tafsir of this very verse and translates the word as death too. This narration is in the most authentic book after the Holy Quran, under the chapter called “Kitabul Tafsir” (Book of Exegete).

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: {مُتَوَفِّيكَ} مُمِيتُكَ

Ibn Abbas (R.A) said, “Mutawaffika (مُتَوَفِّيكَ) means death.”

[Sahih al-Bukhari p.745]

Refutations of Non-Ahmadi Argument

Argument 1:

The word مُتَوَفِّیۡکَ does not mean death but means to “take” meaning that Allah took Isa (A.S) to heaven physically.

Firstly, we have already proven that Tawaffa does indeed mean to take but as per Quran, Ahadith, and Lexicons when Allah takes a human, it means “taking of the soul“. It never means taking someone with body and soul.

Secondly, even if we assume it means to take with the body, where does it say “taking to heaven”?

Argument 2:

The narration of Ibn Abbas (RA) is weak, even though it is in Sahih Bukhari. There are multiple reasons the give:

1) There is no Isnad (Chain of narrators)

This is an extremely immature allegation of Imam Bukhari (R.H) himself. Why would he meticulously compile the most authentic ahadith that we have ever seen, and yet be so neglectful to add weak narrations with no Isnad? Sunnis will attack anyone just to go against Ahmadis. Nevertheless, according to the Tafsir of Sahih Bukhari, when Imam Bukhari (R.H) leaves the Isnad out, he is personally taking responsibility and commanding it to be authentic.

أكثر البخاري من أحاديث وأقوال الصحابة وغيرهم بغير إسناد فإن كان بصيغة جزم كقال وروى ونحوهما فهو حكم منه بصحته

Most of Al-Bukhari’s hadiths and sayings of the Companions and others without chain of narrators. If it is in the form of assertiveness, such as what Qala (he said), Rawa (he narrated), and the like, then it is a judgment of it, is sahih.

[Umdat al-Qari, Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari, pg 32]

Nevertheless, we will still show the Isnad as is mentioned in multiple books of classical scholars so no excuse is left.

1) Tafsir Al Tabari

ذِكْرُ مَنْ قَالَ ذَلِكَ: حَدَّثَنِي الْمُثَنَّى، قَالَ: ثنا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، قَالَ: ثني مُعَاوِيَةُ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَوْلُهُ: {إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ} [آل عمران: 55] يَقُولُ: «إِنِّي مُمِيتُكَ»

(تفسير جامع البيان في تفسير القرآن، الطبري ت 310 هـ)

2) Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim, Volume 2, Page 661

حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي ثنا أَبُو صَالِحٍ، حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، عن ابن عَبَّاسٍ قَوْلُهُ: إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ يَقُولُ: إِنِّي مُمِيتُكَ

3) Ibn Hajr (R.H)

وقال ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ ” مُتَوَفِّيكَ : مُمِيتُكَ “. قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ : ثنا أَبِي ، ثنا أَبُو صَالِحٍ ، ثنا مُعَاوِيَةُ ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، بِهَذَا.

(تغليق التعليق لابن حجر» كتاب التفسير» من تفسير سورة المائدة 1410/206)

4) Tafseer Ibn Al-Mundhir, Volume 1, Page 221

حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي ثنا أَبُو صَالِحٍ، حَدَّثَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، عن ابن عَبَّاسٍ قَوْلُهُ: إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ يَقُولُ: إِنِّي مُمِيتُكَ

2) This is a Muallaq narration

Another Sunni claim is that the narration is Muallaq and thus not authentic. Muallaq narrations are those that have one or more successive narrators omitted from the beginning of their chain.

This allegation shows an utter lack of knowledge in hadith sciences. Muhaddthin and Sunni scholars agree that Muallaq narrations of Imam Bukhari are indeed authentic if in affirmative or definitive form like Qala (said) or Rawā (narrated). This is the case with the narration of Ibn Abbas (R.A) in Sahih Bukhari as it says “Qala Ibn Abbas”. Here are some of the proofs.

“According to the rules that the ulama’ of hadith have generally upheld, the Mu’allaq aḥadīth of al-Bukhārī are considered as Sahih if the suspension is made in decisive words, such as qala (said), fa’ala (did), amara (commanded), nahā (prohibited), dhakara (mentioned), rawā (narrated) and so on. Suspension (ta liq) would not convey validity and soundness (şihha) if it occurs in a defective form or expression (sighat al-tamrid) such as “it is narrated from so and so” (yurma an kadha wa kadha), “it is said of him” (yuqalu ‘anhu), “it is mentioned, or narrated” (yudhkaru, yuḥkā) and the like, which are in any case usually not employed in the typical cases of ta’liq.”

[A Textbook of Hadith Studies Authenticity, Compilation, Classification and Criticism of Hadith by Mohammad Hashim Kamali, p163]

The two most famous Sunni websites also say the same:

Mu‘allaq Hadeeths in Saheeh Al-Bukhari falls into two categories:

1. Those that he narrated with a definitive form, for example: when he says so-and-so said such-and-such or mentioned such-and-such… This method of narrating Mu‘allaq Hadeeths is considered a judgment by Al-Bukhari that these Hadeeths are authentically attributed to the person they are attributed to. This is because he would never have definitively attributed something to a certain narrator unless he had verified the authenticity of that attribution to that narrator.

2. Those with a less definitive form, for example, when he says, it was said or it was narrated on the authority of so and so… Hadeeths in this form are not necessarily authentic because this form of narration may be also used with Dha‘eef (weak) Hadeeths.

[Islamweb Fatwa (Sunni website)]

From what the scholars have said about the methodology of Imam al-Bukhaari in narrating mu’allaq reports, we can divide his mu’allaq reports (of which there are one hundred and sixty) into two categories:

1- Those which were narrated in a decisive form, such as saying “He narrated…” and so on.

The ruling on these mu’allaq reports is that they are saheeh or hasan, because it is not possible for him to state that in a decisive form unless it was saheeh in his view. Rather there are some reports which meet his conditions but he reported them in mu’allaq form.

The scholars made an exception from this principle in the case of just one hadeeth, which is reported in mu’allaq form in the Book of Zakaah (2/525).

[IslamQA Answer (Sunni Website)]

More references regarding Muallaq narrations in Sahih Bukhari can be found here.

Argument 3:

The word Mutawaffika (مُتَوَفِّیۡکَ) does not mean death but means to “sleep” meaning he was caused to sleep.

Firstly, to claim the meaning that Allah is promising Isa (A.S) to cause him to sleep in this verse will be a mockery of the Quran. He has caused Isa (A.S) to sleep thousands of times before so why would He mention this in a verse specifically in the context of Quran 3:55 of Allah and the disbelievers both planning. Allah causing Isa (A.S) to sleep simply does not fit.

Secondly, let’s look back at the Quran 5:117 where Isa (A.S) uses the word Tawaffa for himself. Let’s look at the verse through the lens of Isa (A.S) sleeping. If we take the meaning of Tawaffa as sleep, then in this context, Isa (A.S) would be saying “I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them, but since Thou didst cause me to SLEEP (tawafaitani), Thou hast been the Watcher over them”.

How is Isa (A.S) being exonerated in this verse by mentioning that since he was asleep, he does not know the condition of his people? How is sleep a good excuse for not knowing the misguidance of his people? How is this in the realm of reason by any standard?! What makes it even more absurd is that this is the statement of Isa (A.S) on the day of judgment.

Thirdly, even if we take it to mean sleep, then his body is still asleep while the soul is alive in heaven which the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) saw on Mairaj. This means his soul and body are separated for at least 600 years.

Fourthly, the strongest proof that it cannot mean sleep is that we have already shown 3 authentic narrations that show the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W), Ali (R.A), and all prophets will use the word Tawaffa similarly, at the same time, in same context, and same place, i.e., the Day of Judgement. We know that Ali RA and the rest of the Prophets (A.S) have died. Why should we take this baseless interpretation against the clear interpretation in Sahih Ahadith? Read more on it here.

Argument 4:

When they cannot prove مُتَوَفِّیۡکَ means to “take me”, they claim that it means death BUT it will happen on the 2nd coming. To back that up they quote a famous tafsir by Imam Suyuti and Imam Tabari which has this weak narration:

عن ابن عباس في قوله { إني متوفيك ورافعك } يعني رافعك ثم متوفيك في آخر الزمان

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas about the Ayah “I’ll take you and raise you”; “It means I’ll raise you then will cause you to die near the End of Times.”

Firstly, this narration contradicts Quran 5:117 where Isa’s (A.S) death is mentioned in his first coming rather than the second. Check here.

Secondly, this view contradicts the belief of Ibn Abbas (R.A) himself as we have shown earlier. Check here.

Thirdly, this narration is weak as Sa’id ibn Juwabyr and Ad Dahak are weak narrators.

Fourthly, Ad Dahak never met Ibn Abbas (R.A).

Finally, this narration is weaker than the one quoted above. We quoted Sahih Bukhari’s narration which has a seal of authenticity by Imam Bukhari(R.H) himself while they are quoting one from Durr Manthur to counter it. Sahih Bukhari is the most authentic book after the Holy Quran. In comparison, Durr Manthur is not even part of the Sihae Sitta (6 most authentic books of hadith).

Argument 5:

When non-Ahmadis fail to prove mutawaffika means to take someone, or death only on the 2nd coming, they bring up another argument. They call it Taqdim Wa Tahkir meaning the “Rafa” of Isa (A.S) happened before his Tawaffi, thus they change the order with which it is mentioned in the Quran. This means that Tawaffa does indeed mean to die, but it will happen after his rafa (exaltation). In short, Isa (A.S) will be lifted to heaven alive, then sent back in the latter days, when he will die.

Let us quote the verse and see the order in which Allah chose the verse to be:

“When Allah said, ‘O Jesus,I will cause thee to die a natural death and will exalt thee to Myself, and will clear thee from the charges of those who disbelieve, and will place those who follow thee above those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me shall be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ”

[Quran 3:56]

As seen, the order in which Allah described the sequence of events is that Isa’s (AS) tawaffi happened first then his exaltation. Yet the non-Ahmadis persist in changing Allah’s order.

Their first attempt is to quote a weak narration attributed to Ibn Abbas, through Ad-Dahaak and Saeed Ibn juwaybir, who have unanimously been declared weak when reporting from Ibn Abbas. Some scholars who have rejected these narrators include Ahmad Ibn Hanbal, Al-Dhahabi, Imam an-Nasai and Imam al-Dar Qutni. These are 1% of the evidence for how this narration is very weak, however it will not be further expounded here.

Nevertheless, the non-Amazis cannot attribute this belief to Ibn Abbas, the greatest mufassir of the Quran.

They are now left to their thoughts, and their only thought now is to state “The order is switched just because it sounds nice to me”; if the non-Amazis simply ponder over this they would leave this belief at once. However, the false notion will still be refuted in several ways.

1) The Christians went astray only after Isa AS’s Tawaffi.

Detailed response: Isa AS’s Tawaffi is mentioned twice in the Quran. Once at 3:55, and the other at 5:117 during judgment day. 5:117 states that:

“I said nothing to them except that which Thou didst command me—‘Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.’ And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them, but since Thou caused my Tawaffa, Thou hast been the Watcher over them; and Thou art Witness over all things.”

From this verse many things are clear:

• Isa AS testified that his people were upon Tawheed as long as he remained among them preaching. (I said nothing to them except that which Thou didst command me—‘Worship Allah, my Lord, and your Lord.’ And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them)

• It was only after Allah did the tawaffi of Isa AS, that he was not amongst his people anymore.

After pondering over this, there is no reason for a non-Ahmadi to still hold this position. However, this false notion will still be refuted through a different angle:

2) Allah raises the status of humans, so even if we were to switch Tawaffi and Rafaa, it would mean that Allah would first exalt the status of Isa AS, then he would take his soul at death.

This would be in line with the Quranic verse:

These Messengers have We exalted, some of them above others: among them there are those to whom Allah spoke; and some of them He exalted by degrees of rank. (2:254)

If we were to entertain this false notion of Taqdim wa Takhir, Isa AS’s Rafa would be the rafaa of this verse, meaning that he was exalted in rank, then Allah took his soul at death. So, even for argument’s sake if this notion was accepted, it would still not support the physical ascent and descent of Isa AS.

In conclusion, the Non-Ahmadis should truly ponder over how ridiculous this notion. If they switch the order of Tawaffi and Rafaa, what is stopping them from switching the order of the other parts of the verse?

“and will clear thee from the charges of those who disbelieve, and will place those who follow thee above those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me shall be your return, and I will judge between you concerning that wherein you differ”.

Why do the Non-Ahmadis not place the last part of the verse at the beginning, and what right do they have to say someone is wrong if they choose to do something like that?

The true meaning of the verse is that Allah will cause Isa AS to die, then raise his status.

Introduction

Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul.

It never means the taking of the body & soul.

Non-Ahmadi debaters frequently confuse two distinct Arabic grammatical forms: Tawaffā (تَوَفَّى) and Tuwuffiya (تُوُفِّيَ, often colloquially written as Tuwaffa).

Some claim that because one is active and the other is passive, their theological meanings must be completely different. This argument is rooted in basic ignorance of Arabic grammar. Both forms refer strictly to death and the taking of the soul.

The Grammatical Distinction

In Arabic grammar, the difference between these two words is simply a matter of active versus passive voice:

• Active Voice (Tawaffā — تَوَفَّى): This is the active verb meaning “He took the soul” or “He caused to die.” The Actor is Allah. When Allah causes a human being to die, He does Tawaffā.

• Passive Voice (Tuwuffiya — تُوُفِّيَ): This is the passive verb meaning “He was caused to die” or “He passed away.” The person who dies undergoes Tuwuffiya.

In classical Arabic, you never say Tawaffā Zayd to mean “Zayd died.” Zayd did not take his own soul! Instead, classical Arabs say Tuwuffiya Zayd (“Zayd was caused to die”).

Allah alone is Al-Mutawaffī (the One who causes death), and the human being is Al-Mutawaffā (the one whose soul is taken).

The Rule in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55)

In Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55), Allah addresses Isa (AS):

إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ

“When Allah said: O Isa, I will cause you to die [Mutawaffīka] and will exalt you to Myself.”

[Quran 3:55]

The word Mutawaffīka is the active participle (Ism Fā‘il) derived from Tawaffā. Allah Himself is the Actor. He is informing Isa (AS) that He will take his soul and cause him to die a natural death.

Neither the active form (Tawaffā) nor the passive form (Tuwuffiya) ever means physical bodily ascension into heaven.

There is zero verse in the Holy Quran, zero Hadith, and zero Arabic dictionary where either form means lifting flesh and bones into the sky.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Tawaffa and Tuwuffiya?

Tawaffā is the active verb (Allah causes a person to die and takes their soul). Tuwuffiya is the passive verb (the person was caused to die / passed away). Both denote death.

Why do people say “Tuwaffa”?

“Tuwaffa” is a common colloquial mispronunciation of the classical passive verb Tuwuffiya.

Does either form mean bodily ascension?

No. In both active and passive forms, when applied to human beings, it strictly denotes the departure of the soul. It never means taking the physical body.

Introduction

Non-Ahmadis often claim that we are making up new translations of the Holy Quran regarding the verses that prove the death of Isa (A.S). Although these allegations do not matter since we have proved our case from the Quran, Ahadith, ijmah (consensus) of sahaba (R.A), statements of Salaf-us-Saliheen, and Arabic lexicons, it is a good exercise to shut the critics on all fronts.

The Foundational Rule: Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul. It never means the taking of the body & soul. For a complete theological and linguistic breakdown, see our master guide: What Does Tawaffa (توفى) Mean in Islam?.

Below are over 50 non-Ahmadi Qur’an translations proving that even non-Ahmadi scholars and translators agree that Tawaffa signifies death.

Introduction

The Arabic verb تَوَفَّى (tawaffa) is vital to the Islamic discourse on the death of Isa (AS). It’s correct interpretation carries significant theological weight.

Taking of the Soul: Death or Sleep

The root word wafā (وفى) means “to complete,” “to take in full,” or “to receive fully.” The verb tawaffa literally means to take completely or in full. Several classical lexicons, like Lisan al-Arab and Lane’s Lexicon, confirm this root meaning.

When Allah (subject/فاعل) does the Tawaffi of a human (object /مفعول), it ONLY means taking of the soul. This can be 1) at the time of death, or 2) sleep if night is mentioned. There is NO other meaning for it. It NEVER means taking of the body and soul or flying towards Allah.

Usage in Qur’an

Tawaffa has been used 25 times in the Qur’an. The list of the ayahs are listed below:

2:234; 2:240; 3:55; 3:193; 4:15; 4:97; 5:117; 6:61; 7:37; 7:126; 8:50; 10:46; 10:104; 12:101; 13:40; 16:28; 16:32; 16:70; 22:5; 32:11; 40:67; 40:77; 47:27; 6:60; 39:42

In verses 6:60 and 39:42, night or sleep is mentioned which causes it to refer to sleep. ALL other uses of Tawaffa in the Quran are in reference to death.

Verse 39:42

In 39:42, Tawaffa is used for the same two distinct states, as mentioned above.

• Death (موت): Permanent cessation of biological life.

• Sleep (نوم): Temporary withdrawal of the soul, where the body remains alive.

اَللّٰہُ یَتَوَفَّی الۡاَنۡفُسَ حِیۡنَ مَوۡتِہَا وَالَّتِیۡ لَمۡ تَمُتۡ فِیۡ مَنَامِہَا ۚ فَیُمۡسِکُ الَّتِیۡ قَضٰی عَلَیۡہَا الۡمَوۡتَ وَیُرۡسِلُ الۡاُخۡرٰۤی اِلٰۤی اَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّی ؕ اِنَّ فِیۡ ذٰلِکَ لَاٰیٰتٍ لِّقَوۡمٍ یَّتَفَکَّرُوۡنَ

Allah takes away the souls of human beings at the time of their death; and during their sleep of those also that are not yet dead. And then He retains those against which He has decreed death, and sends back the others till an appointed term. In that surely are Signs for a people who reflect.
[Quran: 39:42]

Here, yatawaffā (یَتَوَفَّی) is used both for actual death and for the temporary taking of the soul during sleep, as the word sleep is mentioned.

Non-Ahmadi Allegations

Tawaffa can mean sleep so Isa (AS) is asleep in the heavens

Some ignorant anti-ahmadis argue that because Tawaffa can also mean “sleep” (temporary taking of the soul), therefore, Isa (AS) may simply be sleeping in heaven for 2000+ years, awaiting his return. They argue that Allah first made Isa (AS) fall asleep, then raised him up. They claim that this ‘logically’ means Isa (AS) is still alive in heaven rather than having passed away.

Refutation: Tawaffa of Isa (AS) is death

Besides being a clear insult to the wisdom and power of Allah, the argument made by some anti-Ahmadis that Tawaffa in the case of Isa (AS) means “sleep” is neither supported by the Qur’an nor by any sound reasoning. Anti-Ahmadis are so lost and desperate that they invent absurd scenarios to keep Isa (AS) alive, completely misrepresenting the meaning of Tawaffa in verses like 3:55 and 5:117. As clearly stated before, when Allah performs Tawaffa on a being with a soul, such as human, it refers to death only, unless sleep or night is explicitly mentioned. In verses 3:55 and 5:117, there is NO mention of sleep or night. The only logical, textual meaning is death, yet anti-Ahmadis twist it to mean sleep without any linguistic or contextual justification. This is outright a lie against Allah.

Not only does their belief contradict these verses, but it also flies in the face of the Qur’an’s universal law of mortality, as seen in 3:144 (“All messengers before Muhammad have passed away”) and 3:185 (“Every soul shall taste death”).

Their position contradicts not only the Qur’an, but also the established usages of Tawaffa in Hadith. This is not to mention the fact that how their own scholars have translated these same verses over centuries as referring to death and NOT sleep.

Finally, the claim that Isa (AS) merely fell asleep to be saved from his enemies is completely illogical. If the threat to Isa (AS) was death at the hands of his enemies, what kind of “rescue” is sleep? Would that not make him even more vulnerable? This entire argument lacks Qur’anic, linguistic, and rational credibility, and shows the lengths to which our opponents will go to avoid accepting the clear truth that Isa (AS) has passed away.

Khalifatul Masih IV (RH) explains

Hazrat Khalifatul Masih IV, Mirza Tahir Ahmad (RH), explains beautifully that although Tawaffa can refer to either death or sleep when the subject (فاعل) is Allah and object (مفعول) is human, it defies human logic that Allah the Exalted would respond to a murder plot of the Jews by making Isa (AS) fall asleep. He explains:

So instead of removing him from the place of danger, God further made him incapable of defending himself? A man who is not asleep could run away but a man who has fallen asleep at the time of danger offers himself as a sitting duck for anybody to shoot him. This meaning is purposeless. It [Verse 39:42] only means that the Tawaffa takes place in two ways: either in the form of death or in the form of sleep.

[Liqa Ma al-Arab, 13th May, 1997]

Thus, as Khalifatul Masih IV (RH) explains, it would be an absolute mockery of God if he had made Isa (AS) fall alseep during the most critically dangerous time of his life. It would have also solved nothing, as all it would have done is put Isa (AS) in more danger.

Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) failed his Tawaffa challenge

Some ignorant non-ahmadis also falsely allege that Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) “failed” his Tawaffa challenge as he ignored that Tawaffa can also mean sleep. They allege that Ahmad (AS) challenged everyone to prove from the Qur’an or Hadith if Tawaffa regarding Isa (AS) meant anything other than death or taking of the soul. They argue that Tawaffa also means ‘sleep’ according to Quran 39:42, so Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) “failed” his so-called challenge.

Refutation

This allegation is a gross misrepresentation. The Promised Messiah (AS) never denied that Tawaffa can refer to sleep. His actual challenge was for anyone to prove that Tawaffa, when used by Allah in reference to a human, means anything other than i) death or ii) the taking of the soul. Since sleep, by definition as stated in Qur’an 39:42, involves the temporary removal (taking) of the soul, it fully falls within the scope of this challenge. Therefore, the objection is very clearly baseless and the challenge of Masih Maud (AS) remains unmet.

Conclusion

In conclusion, Tawaffa can mean sleep, when the aforementioned prerequisite context are met. However, the claim of the anti-ahmadis that Isa (AS) was made to sleep and then raised alive is a very weak and unsupported attempt to avoid the clear Qur’anic teaching of his natural death. In addition, the allegation that Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) “failed” his challenge is not just a clear lie against Ahmad (AS), but also upon Allah and the Quran as well. May Allah give Hidayah to the Anti-Ahmadis.

Introduction

Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul.

It never means the taking of the body & soul.

Some non-Ahmadi Muslims claim that Tawaffa means “to take fully,” and therefore Allah took Isa (AS) physically with his body and soul into heaven.

This claim is false. Tawaffa never means taking the physical body.

What Does Allah Take? (The Quranic Proof)

Whenever Allah takes a human being, He only takes the soul. The Holy Quran clearly establishes this rule:

اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا

“Allah takes away the souls of human beings at the time of their death; and of those that are not yet dead, during their sleep.”

[Quran 39:42]

The verse states that Allah takes the souls (al-anfus). It never says He takes the physical body.

Whether at death or during sleep, it is strictly the soul that is taken. The physical body remains on this earth.

The Zero-Proof Challenge (Burden of Proof)

There is zero verse in the Holy Quran and zero Hadith in all of Islamic literature where Allah takes a human being and it means taking their physical body.

Whoever claims that “take fully” means taking the physical body carries the entire burden of proof.

They must produce a single verse from the Quran or a single authentic Hadith where Allah does the Tawaffa of a human and it means taking their body. There is zero.

What Arabic Lexicons Actually Say

Classical Arabic dictionaries are completely unanimous. In Lisān al-ʿArab, the most famous Arabic lexicon, it states:

تَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ إِذَا قَبَضَ نَفْسَهُ

“Allah caused him to die [Tawaffāhu Allāh] when He took his soul.”

[Lisan al-Arab, vol. 14, p. 440]

There is zero Arabic lexicon stating that when Allah takes a human, He takes their physical body into the sky.

No. When Allah takes a human being, He only takes the soul (at death or during sleep). It never means taking the physical body.

In Arabic, when Allah takes a human, it refers strictly to receiving their soul. There is zero evidence in the Quran or Hadith that it means taking the physical body.

Hadith #1

حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الْعَلَّافُ الْمِصْرِيُّ، ثنا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ، ثنا نَافِعُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، حَدَّثَنِي عُمَارَةُ بْنُ غَزِيَّةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، أَنَّ أُمَّهُ، فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ حُسَيْنٍ حَدَّثَتْهُ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ كَانَتْ تَقُولُ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي مَرَضِهِ الَّذِي قُبِضَ فِيهِ، قَالَ لِفَاطِمَةَ: «يَا بُنَيَّةُ احْنِي عَلَيَّ» فَأَحْنَتْ عَلَيْهِ فَنَاجَاهَا سَاعَةً ثُمَّ انْكَشَفَتْ وَهِيَ تَبْكِي وَعَائِشَةُ حَاضِرَةٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِسَاعَةٍ: «احْنِي عَلَيَّ يَا بُنَيَّةُ» فَأَحْنَتْ عَلَيْهِ فَنَاجَاهَا سَاعَةً ثُمَّ انْكَشَفَتْ عَنْهُ فَضَحِكَتْ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَقُلْتُ: أَيْ بُنَيَّةُ، أَخْبِرِينِي مَاذَا نَاجَاكِ أَبُوكِ؟ فَقَالَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: نَاجَانِي عَلَى حَالٍ سِرٍّ، ظَنَنْتِ أَنِّي أُخْبِرُ بِسِرِّهِ وَهُوَ حَيٌّ فَشَقَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ أَنْ يَكُونَ سِرًّا دُونَهَا، فَلَمَّا قَبَضَهُ اللهُ، قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ لِفَاطِمَةَ: يَا بُنَيَّةُ، أَلَا تُخْبِرينِي بِذَلِكَ الْخَبَرِ؟ قَالَتْ: أَمَّا الْآنَ، فَنَعَمْ، نَاجَانِي فِي الْمَرَّةِ الْأُولَى فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَنَّ جِبْرِيلَ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ يُعَارِضُهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ مَرَّةً، وَأَنَّهُ عَارَضَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ الْعَامَ مَرَّتَيْنِ، وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ نَبِيٌّ إِلَّا عَاشَ نِصْفَ عُمَرَ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُ، وَأَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَنِي أَنَّ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ عَاشَ عِشْرِينَ وَماِئةَ سَنَةٍ وَلَا أُرَانِي إِلَّا ذَاهِبًا عَلَى رَأْسِ السِّتِّينَ فَأَبْكَانِي ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: «يَا بُنَيَّةُ، إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ نِسَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ امْرَأَةٌ أَعْظَمُ رُزِّيَّةً مِنْكِ، فَلَا تَكُونِي أَدْنَى مِنِ امْرَأَةٍ صَبْرًا» وَنَاجَانِي فِي الْمَرَّةِ الْآخِرَةِ فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَنِّي أَوَّلُ أَهْلِهِ لُحُوقًا بِهِ وَقَالَ: «إِنَّكِ سَيِّدَةُ نِسَاءِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ إِلَّا مَا كَانَ مِنَ الْبَتُولِ مَرْيَمَ بِنْتِ عِمْرَانَ» فَضَحِكَتُ بِذَلِكَ

Nawab Siddiq Hassan Khan

ره ورعطریضتی بالقران العام مزین اخبری از امین نبی الاعاش عضت الذمی قبل ما نبری ان سے بنایم ماست عنی باید سنا لان الاناسیاست اسرایتین رجاله بالثقات و له طریق تمام بت در بدت دی

“Narrators are trustworthy (thiqa)….”

[Atharul Qiyamah fi Hajajul Qramah, pg 428]

Imam Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Saalihi al-Shami

Regarding the Fatimah (R.A) chain, he says,

“وروي الطبراني والحاكم والطحاوي والبيهفي سند صحيح”

“Narrated by Tabarani, Al-Hakim, Tahawi and Bayhuti that the chain of narrators is Sahih”

[Subalul Huda wa Irshaad fi sirat Khairul Ibaad, pg 230]

Imam Al-Bayhaqi

Imām al-Bayhaqī (R.H) considers it Sahih.

This is because he does not reject this narration in his book Dala’il al-Nubuwwah, pg 166. Rather, he does taweel (interprets) it in light of the narration by Ibn Al-Musab and Wahb Ibn Munabbih where they say Isa (A.S) died at the age of 32 or 33, respectively. He says after his descent, Isa (A.S) will complete the remaining years of his life and die at the age of 120.

Although we don’t agree with the taweel of Imam Al-Bayhaqi, we only quote it to prove that the narration is not Daif (weak) or Ghareeb (strange). As if it was weak, he would have not done taweel (interpretation) but would have rejected it completely!

Hadith #2

Along with the previous hadith that clearly establishes the age of Isa (A.S) to be 120 at the time of death, we have another similar hadith but without the age mentioned. This is narrated from a different chain than the above.

حدثنا علي بن عبد العزيز ، ثنا أبو نعيم ، ثنا كامل أبو العلاء ، قال : سمعت حبيب بن أبي ثابت ، يحدث عن يحيى بن جعدة ، عن زيد بن أرقم ، قال : خرجنا مع رسول الله – صلى الله عليه وسلم – حتى انتهينا إلى غدير خم أمر بدوح فكسح في يوم ما أتى علينا يوم كان أشد حرا منه ، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه [ ص: 172 ] وقال : “ يا أيها الناس إنه لم يبعث نبي قط إلا عاش نصف ما عاش الذي كان قبله ، وإني أوشك أن أدعى فأجيب ، وإني تارك فيكم ما لن تضلوا بعده كتاب الله ” ثم قام وأخذ بيد علي – رضي الله عنه – فقال : ” يا أيها الناس من أولى بكم من أنفسكم ؟ ” قالوا : الله ورسوله أعلم ، قال من كنت مولاه فعلي مولاه

“Verily, a Prophet was never sent except that he lived for half the lifespan of the Prophet who preceded him.”

[Al Mu’jam Al Kabir Tabarani, 172, 4986]

Explanation 1

It shows that every prophet lives ATLEAST half of the age of the previous prophet. If Isa (A.S) is alive as of now, his age would be 2000 years. For Muhammad (S.A.W) to be a prophet of Allah, he has to live at least half of that i.e 1000 years. Since he died at age 63/64, he is not a prophet of Allah as per the non-Ahmadi Muslims who believe Isa (A.S) is still alive, Nauthibillah.

Common Misconception

Some people believe that every prophet HAS TO live exactly half the age of the previous prophet. For example:

• If Muhammad (S.A.W) – 60 years

• Then Isa (A.S) – 120 years

• And Yahya (A.S) – 240 years

And so on…

However, this is not a correct understanding of the hadith. The hadith only proves that Allah guarantees that the prophet lives at least half the age of the previous prophet. For example: If the Prophet before Isa (as) lived to let’s say 100 years, then him living to 120 still goes past 50.

Explanation 2

Another explanation is that this rule of half age of the prophet is not a general rule but it only applies to Muhammad (S.A.W) and Isa (A.S) because such examples can be from ahadith.

This was said in regard to Prophet’s inheritance. Muhammad (S.A.W) says,

“Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said. ‘We (Apostles) do not bequeath anything to our heirs, but whatever we leave is to be given in charity.’ And by that Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) meant himself.’ The group said, ‘(No doubt), he said so.‘ `Umar then faced `Ali and `Abbas and said, ‘Do you both know that Allah’s Messenger (ﷺ) said that?’ They replied, ‘(No doubt), he said so.’”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 5358]

As seen from the above example, Sahabas quote a general principle stated by Muhammad (S.A.W), however, they know it only applied to himself because we have 2 prophets mentioned in Quran who had heirs.

1) Dawud (A.S)

“And Solomon was heir to David.”

Quran 27:16

2) Zakarya (A.S)

“This is an account of the mercy of thy Lord shown to His servant, Zachariah. When he called upon his Lord, crying in secret. He said, ‘My Lord, the bones have indeed waxed feeble in me, and the head glistens with hoariness but never, my Lord, have I been unblessed in my prayer to Thee; And I fear my relations after me, and my wife is barren. Grant me, therefore, a successor from Thyself, That he may be heir to me and heir to the House of Jacob. And make him, my Lord well-pleasing to Thee.’”

Quran 19:2

So now we know that prophets can leave the heirs and the statement of Muhammad (S.A.W) is not a general rule but it only applies to himself as agreed by the Sahabas (R.A) in the Bukhari narration.

In fact, Hazrat Hakeem-ul-Ummat Maulana Hafiz Noor-ad-Deen (RA) endorsed explanation two which has been given above.

The Following Prophet’s age being half that of the previous Prophet

نبی کی عمر پہلے نبی سے نصف

سوال ۔!السلام علیکم ورحمۃ اللہ

حضرت مسیح موعود نے ایک جگہ وہ حدیث لکھی ہے جس میں ہے کہ نبی کی عمر پہلے سے نصف ہوتی ہے ۔ غالبا وہ یوں ہے انـه لـم يـكـن نبـي إلا عـاش نصف عمر الذي كان قبله و انـه أخبرني أن عيسى بن مريم عليهما السّلام عاش عشرين ومائة سنة ولا أراني إلا ذاهبا لى رأس ستين (الاحاد و المثاني النساء فاطمة ابنة رسول اللہ ) ۔ اس پر بعض لوگ کہتے ہیں کہ یہ حدیث عقل کے خلاف ہے ۔حضورفر ماو میں کیا جواب دیا جاوے۔ اکمل علی اللہ عنہ

جواب۔ صحیح حدیث پر اٹکل بازی کرنا چکڑالویوں ، نیچریوں کا طرز ہے ۔ صحت پر محدثانہ بحث ہونی چاہئے ۔ انبیاء کے اقسام ہیں ۔ حدیث میں یہ مذکور نہیں کہ کس کس قسم کے انبیاء میں یہ نسبت ہوتی ہے۔تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض (البقرۃ:۱۵۴) سے امتیاز ظاہر ہوتا ہے ۔ ہر حدیث کی تکذیب کرنا چکڑالویوں کا کام ہے ۔مومن کا بی طریق نہیں ۔ والسلام

کیا کسی نے اس کو وضعی کہا ہے اور کہنے والا ائمہ حدیث سے ہے۔

والسلام

نورالدین

Hadith #3

There is another hadith that contains the same words and is again mentioned by Imam Al-Tabarani in his book Al Mu’jam Al Kabir. This is a different chain with Hudhaifa bin Usaid Al Ghifari. The chain is as follows:

Muḥammad b. ‘Abd Allāh al-Ḥadramī and Zakariyyāh b. Yaḥ yā al-Sājī – Naṣr b. ‘Abd al-Raḥmanal-Washā – A ḥmad b. al-Qāsim b. Musāwar al-Jawharī and Sa’īd b. Sulaymān al-Wāsiṭ ī – Zayd b.al-Ḥasan al-Anmāṭ ī – Ma’rūf b. Kharbūz – Abū al-Ṭufayl –Ḥudhayfah b. Usayd al-Ghiffārī

حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله الحضرمي وزكريا بن يحيى الساجي ، قالا : ثنا نصر بن عبد الرحمن الوشاء ، ح . وحدثنا أحمد بن القاسم بن مساور الجوهري ، ثنا سعيد بن سليمان الواسطي ، قالا : ثنا زيد بن الحسن الأنماطي ، ثنا معروف بن خربوذ ، عن أبي الطفيل ، عن حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري ، قال : لما صدر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من حجة الوداع نهى أصحابه عن شجرات بالبطحاء متقاربات أن ينزلوا تحتهن ، ثم بعث إليهن فقم ما تحتهن من الشوك ، وعمد إليهن فصلى تحتهن ، ثم قام فقال : ” يا أيها الناس ، إني قد نبأني اللطيف الخبير أنه لم يعمر نبي إلا نصف عمر الذي يليه من قبله ، وإني لأظن أني يوشك أن أدعى فأجيب ، وإني مسئول ، وإنكم مسئولون ، فماذا أنتم قائلون ؟ ” قالوا : نشهد أنك قد بلغت وجاهدت ونصحت ، فجزاك الله خيرا .

فقال : ” أليس تشهدون أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله ، وأن جنته حق وناره حق ، وأن الموت حق ، وأن البعث بعد الموت حق ، وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها ، وأن الله يبعث من في القبور ؟ ” قالوا : بلى ، نشهد بذلك . قال : ” اللهم اشهد ” .

ثم قال : ” أيها الناس ، إن الله مولاي ، وأنا مولى المؤمنين ، وأنا أولى بهم من أنفسهم ، فمن كنت مولاه فهذا مولاه – يعني عليا – اللهم وال من والاه ، وعاد من عاداه ” .

ثم قال : ” يا أيها الناس ، إني فرطكم ، وإنكم واردون علي الحوض ، حوض أعرض ما بين بصرى وصنعاء ، فيه عدد النجوم قدحان من فضة ، وإني سائلكم حين تردون علي عن الثقلين ، فانظروا كيف تخلفوني فيهما ، الثقل الأكبر كتاب الله عز وجل ، سبب طرفه بيد الله ، وطرفه بأيديكم ، فاستمسكوا به لا تضلوا ولا تبدلوا ، وعترتي أهل بيتي ، فإنه نبأني اللطيف الخبير أنهما لن ينقضيا حتى يردا علي الحوض

“When the Messenger of Allāh, peace be upon him, returned from the Farewell Ḥajj, he stoppedHis Ṣaḥābah are a group of trees and asked them to camp under them. Then he sent a messenger to them (i.e. the trees) to pick the thorns under them. Then he went to them, and prayed under them. Then he stood up and said, “O mankind! The Compassionate All-Knowing (Allāh) has informed me that a prophet never lives beyond half the age of the one before him. I think I will be called (soon) and I will answer. I will be questioned (by Allāh) and you too will be questioned. So, what will you say (in reply when you are questioned)?” They said, “We testify that you conveyed (the Message of Allāh to us), and you made jihād and guided us. May Allāh reward you with good.”

[Al Mu’jam Al Kabir Tabarani, vol. 3, p.180, #3052]

Authenticity of Hadith #3

This hadith is either Sahih on the standard of Ibn Hibban and Darussalam or at least Hassan by the standards of Imam Tirmidhi.

Albani has criticized this narration due to only one narrator Al-Anmati quoting Abu Hatim’s words. Before we refute him, here is what others have to say about Al-Anmati.

Tirmidhi

He quotes a chain with Zaid bin Al Hasan Al-Anmati in the hadith and grades it Hasan Ghareeb which is basically Hasan grading.

(Sunan al-Tirmidhī, vol. 5, p. 662, # 3786)

Darussalam

Darussalam grades the same Tirmidhi narration with the same Al-Anmati as Sahih.

Ibn Hibban

He calls Zaid bin Al Hasan Al-Anmati Thiqa (trustworthy). Check the Albani quote below.

Refuting Albani’s criticism of Zaid bin Al Hasan Al-Anmati

Now that we have shown 3 sources calling Al-Anmati trustworthy, let’s see if the criticism of Albani holds any weight. This is what he says:

“This chain is ḍa’īf, due to this al-Anmati. Abū Ḥātim said: “ Munkar al-ḥadīth”. As for Ibn Ḥibbān, he has mentioned him in al-Thiqāt (The Trustworthy Narrators)! But, al-Ḥāfiz gave no weight to it. So, he said in al-Taqrīb: “Ḍa’īf ”.

The ḥadīth has been recorded fully by al-Haythamī (9/164-165) from the report of al-Ṭabarānī in the hadīth of Ḥudhayfah b. Usayd, and he faulted it through this al-Anmāṭ ī, except that he (also) quoted the statement of Abū Ḥātim and Ibn Ḥibbān about him.”

[Silsilah al-Aḥādīth al-Ḍa’īfah wa al- Mawḍ ū’ah wa Atharihah al-Sayyiah fī al-Ummah, vol. 10, p. 679-680, # 4961]

But this criticism by Albani is invalid since he ignores the opinion of Ibn Hibban who calls the same narrator Thiqa. Rather he picks Abu Hatim’s opinion only when we know from Ibn Hajar that when it comes to Abu Hatim’s opinion on any narrator, always pick the opinion of someone else that calls the narrator reliable. This is because Abu Hatim is extremely picky about each narrator. He says it here:

“In al-Mīzān, it is stated that Abū Ḥātim said “He is not accepted as a ḥujjah”. But, watch that carefully. There is stubbornness in Abū Ḥātim. He (the narrator) has been accepted as a ḥujjah by the majority.”

[Hadī al-Sārī Muqaddimah Fatḥ al-Bārī, p. 441]

Imām al-Dhahabī provides says the same about Abu Hatim:

“If Abū Ḥātim declares a narrator to be thiqah(trustworthy), then hold fast to his statement, because he never declares a narrator to be thiqah except a narrator whose a ḥādīth are ṣaḥīḥ. If he weakens a narrator, or says about him “he is not accepted as a ḥujjah”, then pause until you have seen what others have said about him (i.e. that narrator). If there is A SINGLE other person who declares him (i.e. the narrator) to be thiqah (trustworthy), then do not adopt the criticism of Abū Ḥātim, because he is stubborn in rijāl.”

[Siyar A’lām al- Nubalā, vol. 13, p. 260, # 129]

So as seen above, even this narration of Ḥudhayfah b. Usayd al-Ghiffārī is Sahih or at least Hasan and no one can deny our Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) has said these words.

Conclusion

In this article, we showed that the narrations regarding the death of Isa (A.S) at the age of 120 are

• Sahih and we see them in multiple different chains with different narrators. Thus they are mutawatir.

• They are authenticated by numerous scholars.

• Even if someone ever proves 1 chain as Daif (weak), other chains still stand.

We also proved that the saying “Every prophet lives half the age of the prophet” can mean 2 things.

• Every prophet reaches half the age of the previous prophet. This is one of the signs of the truthfulness of a prophet. They can go beyond the half-age mark, but reaching half is a guarantee by Allah.

• The statement only applies to Muhammad (S.A.W) and Isa (A.S). It does not apply to all prophets as Muhammad (S.A.W) has said similar things in the example hadith we provided above where the general rule is said but only applies to him.

Frequently Asked Questions

What hadith mentions that Prophet Isa (Jesus AS) lived to 120 years?

In Kanz al-Ummal and Al-Mu’jam Al-Kabir by Al-Tabarani, Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) stated to his daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA): “Jibreel informed me that every prophet lived half the life of the prophet before him, and Jesus son of Mary lived for one hundred and twenty years.”

What does this narration prove regarding the lifespan of Jesus (AS)?

It proves that Jesus (AS) lived a mortal human lifespan on earth and passed away, rather than remaining physically alive in space for thousands of years.

Introduction

Rafa is an Arabic verb that means to raise or elevate. When Allah raises (Rafa’a) humans, He only raises their souls. Never their bodies.

It never means the physical flight of a human body into the sky.

Whoever claims that Allah raises a living human physically with both body and soul carries the entire burden of proof. There is zero Quranic verse and zero Sahih Hadith in all of Islamic literature that supports such a claim.

The Holy Quran establishes the universal law of human existence on earth in Surah Al-A’raf:

قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ

“He said: Therein shall you live, and therein shall you die, and from it shall you be brought forth.”

[Quran 7:25]

Allah explicitly commands that all human beings live on earth, die on earth, and are resurrected from the earth. No human body is exempt from this universal divine decree.

When the Holy Quran speaks of Allah doing the Rafa of His righteous servants, it refers exclusively to spiritual elevation, honor, high status, and the raising of the soul.

1. Rafa in Arabic Lexicons & Dictionaries

Classical Arabic lexicons are completely unanimous on the root word R-F-`A (ر-ف-ع).

When the verb Rafa’a is used for a human being in relation to Allah, it means elevation in rank, honor, dignity, and spiritual station. It never means transporting physical flesh and bones into outer space.

In Lisān al-ʿArab, the premier dictionary of the Arabic language, Ibn Manzur records:

ورَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ: أَعْلَى ذِكْرَهُ ومَنْزِلَتَهُ

“And Allah raised him: He elevated his remembrance and his station.”

Classical authorities including Tāj al-ʿArūs, Kitāb al-ʿAyn, and Al-Mufradāt by Imam Raghib al-Isfahani confirm this exact principle. When Allah raises a person, He exalts their honor and spiritual grade.

There is zero Arabic lexicon in existence stating that when Allah performs Rafa of a human, He carries their physical body into the heavens.

• Read the comprehensive linguistic analysis: The Usage of Rafa in the Lexicons.

2. Rafa in the Holy Quran (Every Verse Analyzed)

The Holy Quran uses derivatives of Rafa dozens of times across different contexts.

Whenever the Holy Quran speaks of Allah raising human beings, it signifies elevation in spiritual ranks and honor:

وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٍ

“And some of them He exalted by degrees of rank.”

[Quran 2:253]

Similarly, Allah describes how He elevates believers and prophets:

يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ

“Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those to whom knowledge is given, to high ranks.”

[Quran 58:11]

Every single occurrence of Rafa in the Quran regarding human beings refers to spiritual elevation, rank, status, or soul. Not a single verse speaks of a living human body being launched into the clouds.

• Read the full verse-by-verse breakdown: The Usage of Rafa in The Qur’an.

3. Rafa in Hadith Literature

In the authentic Hadith literature, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeatedly used the word Rafa.

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught Muslims to pray for Rafa multiple times every single day. In every rak’ah of prayer, sitting between the two prostrations (Sajdah), the Holy Prophet ﷺ recited this supplication:

رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَاجْبُرْنِي وَارْزُقْنِي وَارْفَعْنِي

“O Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, improve my situation, grant me provision, and raise me [Warfa’ni].”

[Sunan Ibn Majah 898]

Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Allah to physically hoist him into the sky five times a day? Absolutely not. He was asking for spiritual elevation, dignity, and closeness to Allah.

Furthermore, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stated:

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْفَعُ بِهَذَا الْكِتَابِ أَقْوَامًا وَيَضَعُ بِهِ آخَرِينَ

“By this Book, Allah will raise [Yarfa’u] some people and degrade others.”

[Sahih Muslim 817a]

Those whom Allah raises through the Quran are not physically pulled into the sky. Their moral, spiritual, and intellectual status is elevated.

• Read the full Hadith proofs and narrations: The Usage of Rafa’a in Hadith Literature.

4. The Sequence in Quran 3:55: Mutawaffika wa Rafi’uka

The divine sequence in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55) settles the fate of Isa (AS) with complete clarity:

إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَىٰ إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا

“When Allah said: O Jesus, I will cause thee to die a natural death [Mutawaffīka], and will exalt thee to Myself [Rāfi’uka], and will clear thee from the charges of those who disbelieve…”

[Quran 3:55]

Notice the divine chronological sequence:
1. Mutawaffīka: Allah causes Isa (AS) to die a natural death and takes his soul.
2. Rāfi’uka: Allah elevates him spiritually to Himself.
3. Muṭahhiruka: Allah clears his pure name from the false allegations of the disbelievers.

Natural death (Tawaffa) strictly precedes spiritual elevation (Rafa).

Some clerics claim that Rafi’uka happened first and Mutawaffika will happen thousands of years later. This claim is groundless. To invert the direct word order of the Holy Quran without any Quranic textual proof is a clear distortion. Allah first caused Isa (AS) to die naturally, and then exalted his soul to Himself.

• Read the full exegesis and linguistic proof: Quran 3:55: Mutawaffika wa Rafi’uka Explained.

5. Not Crucified & Killed but Raised: Quran 4:157-158 (Flagship Refutation)

The primary verse cited by contemporary clerics to argue for physical bodily ascension is Surah An-Nisa (4:157-158):

وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ … بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا

“And their saying: We did kill the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah; whereas they slew him not, nor crucified him, but he was made to appear to them like one crucified… Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself [Bal Rafa’ahullāhu Ilayh]. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”

[Quran 4:157-158]

Understanding the Historical Context:

The Jewish enemies of Isa (AS) did not merely want him dead; they specifically sought to crucify him. Under Old Testament law, anyone hanged on a tree is deemed accursed of God (Deuteronomy 21:23). Their objective was to prove that Jesus was a false prophet who died an accursed death.

The Linguistic Function of “Bal” (Rather):

In Arabic grammar, the particle Bal (بَلْ) functions as Idrab (rectification). It negates the preceding claim and asserts the direct opposite.
– The Jewish Claim: We humiliated him, proved him accursed, and killed him on the cross.
– The Divine Negation: Bal Rafa’ahullahu Ilayh — Nay, rather Allah exalted his spiritual status and raised him to Himself!

The opposite of an accursed, humiliated death on the cross is not levitating into the stratosphere. The opposite of humiliation and curse is spiritual exaltation, honor, and closeness to Allah.

Furthermore, the verse states Ilayh (“to Himself”). It does not state Ila al-Sama’ (“to the sky”). Allah is not located in the physical atmosphere.

• 👉 Read our comprehensive flagship refutation: The True Meaning of Rafa of Isa (AS) | Quran 4:158 Explained.

6. Allah is Al-Rafi (The Raiser) — One of the 99 Attributes

One of the beautiful 99 attributes of Allah is Al-Rāfi’ (الرافع — The Exalter / The Raiser).

Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d. 505 AH), one of the greatest scholars in Islamic history, wrote in Al-Maqṣad al-Asnā:

الْخَافِضُ الرَّافِعُ: هُوَ الَّذِي يَخْفِضُ الْكُفَّارَ بِالشَّقَاوَةِ وَيَرْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالسَّعَادَةِ، وَيَرْفَعُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ بِالتَّقْرِيبِ إِلَيْهِ

“Al-Khafid, Ar-Rafi: He is the One who abases the unbelievers through misfortune and exalts the believers through blessedness. He exalts His elect by drawing them near to Him.“

[Al-Maqsad al-Asna]

Allah’s attribute of Ar-Rāfi’ does not blast human bodies into the cosmos. He exalts believers by bringing their hearts and souls near to Him through spiritual illumination and divine favor.

• Read the complete study of this divine attribute: Allah is Al-Rafi (The Raiser) | One of 99 Attributes.

7. Allah Does Not Have a Spatial Direction

A fundamental pillar of Islamic theology (Aqeedah) is that Allah is free from physical body, space (Makan), and spatial coordinates.

Allah is not confined to a directional coordinate above the clouds. Surah Al-Baqarah affirms:

وَلِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ ۚ فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ

“To Allah belong the East and the West; so whithersoever you turn, there will be the presence of Allah.”

[Quran 2:115]

If someone claims that Isa (AS) was raised physically toward Allah, they must explain: Where is Allah physically located?

To assert that physical height brings someone closer to Allah is gross anthropomorphism. A person on top of Mount Everest is not geographically closer to Allah than someone in a valley. Spiritual proximity is of the soul, not physical altitude.

• Read the theological refutation of anthropomorphism: Allah Does Not Have a Direction.

8. What is the Isra and Miraj?

Clerics frequently cite the miraculous Ascension (Mi’raj) of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to argue that prophets can travel physically into outer space.

However, the Holy Quran explicitly identifies the Mi’raj as a divine spiritual vision (Ru’ya):

وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِّلنَّاسِ

“And We made not the vision [Ru’yā] which We showed thee but as a trial for men.”

[Quran 17:60]

The Mother of the Believers, Hazrat Aisha (RA), testified to the true spiritual reality of the Ascension:

مَا فُقِدَ جَسَدُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ أَسْرَى بِرُوحِهِ

“The body of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never missing, but Allah caused his soul to journey.”

[Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Surah 17:1]

If the greatest of all creation, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, experienced the Mi’raj as a transcendent spiritual elevation of the soul, how can anyone argue that Isa (AS) was taken up in a physical spaceflight?

• Read the detailed analysis: What is the Isra and Miraj?.

9. The Rafa of Isa (AS) Was Like Ali (RA) and Uthman (RA)

The Companions of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly used the word Rafa to describe death and the elevation of the soul to Allah.

In classical historical chronicles, early Muslims described the martyrdom and passing of Hazrat Ali (RA) and Hazrat Uthman (RA) using the exact term Rafa. Their souls were raised to Allah, while their blessed physical bodies were laid to rest in the earth.

Furthermore, Hazrat Anas bin Malik (RA) stated concerning the passing of the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ:

أَكْرَمَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ نَبِيَّهُ أَنْ يُرِيَهُ فِي أُمَّتِهِ مَا يَكْرَهُ، فَرَفَعَهُ إِلَيْهِ

“Allah honored His Prophet ﷺ by not letting him see in his nation what he would dislike, so He raised him to Himself [Fa-Rafa’ahu Ilayh].”

[Shu’ab al-Iman, 1410]

Hazrat Anas (RA) used the exact same words (Rafa’ahu Ilayh) for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as the Quran used for Isa (AS) in Surah An-Nisa (4:158). Prophet Muhammad’s body remained on earth and was buried in Medina. His soul was raised to Allah.

• Read the historical records of the Companions: The Rafa of Isa Was Like Ali and Uthman.

10. The Rafa of Prophet Idris (AS) Explained

The Holy Quran uses the exact verb Rafa for Prophet Idris (AS) in Surah Maryam:

وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا

“And We raised him to an exalted station.”

[Quran 19:57]

Classical commentators unanimously clarify this verse. Imam al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Makan ‘Aliyyan refers to high spiritual rank, prophetical dignity, and closeness to Allah.

Prophet Idris (AS) was not transported alive to live permanently in outer space. He lived his natural lifespan and passed away on earth like every other prophet of God.

• Read the comparative exegesis: The Rafa of Idris Explained.

11. Refuting the Skylight Myth: Was Isa Raised Through a Roof Window?

In popular medieval folklore, a widespread myth claims that Jesus was trapped in a house surrounded by Roman soldiers, when a roof window opened, and he was physically yanked up to heaven through the ceiling.

This fable has zero foundation in the Holy Quran and zero basis in Sahih Hadith.

It was borrowed directly from fabricated Isrā’īliyyāt (apocryphal Judeo-Christian tales) that penetrated early historical commentaries without chains of authenticity. The Holy Quran gives zero mention of any roof openings or ceiling rescues.

• Read the textual refutation of this fable: Was Isa Raised Through the Roof Window?.

12. Classical Scholarly Consensus & Refuting Physical Rafa

The greatest classical commentators and theological minds of Sunni Islam affirmed that Rafa represents spiritual elevation.

Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (d. 606 AH) writes in his monumental Tafsir al-Kabir regarding Rafi’uka Ilayya:

الْمُرَادُ بِالرَّفْعِ إِلَيْهِ الرَّفْعُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ لَا يَمْلِكُ الْحُكْمَ فِيهِ عَلَيْهِ غَيْرُهُ

“The meaning of raising him to Himself is raising him to a station where none exercises authority over him except Allah.”

[Tafsir al-Kabir, Surah 3:55]

Imam Razi explains that since Allah is transcendent and free from spatial confinement, raising someone “to Allah” cannot be spatial or bodily.

The belief in physical bodily longevity in outer space for thousands of years contradicts the fundamental Quranic nature of human physiology:

وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا خَالِدِينَ

“And We did not make them bodies that ate no food, nor were they to live forever.”

[Quran 21:8]

Prophets possess mortal physical bodies that require nourishment and age on earth. The soul alone is elevated to the divine presence.

• Read classical scholarly quotes: Rafa Explained by Scholars.

• Learn how physical ascension crept into Muslim thought: The Heresy of Physical Rafa.

Summary & Takeaways

• The Definitional Golden Rule: Rafa means to raise or elevate. When Allah raises humans, He only raises their souls. Never their bodies.

• Zero Textual Evidence: There is zero Quranic verse and zero Sahih Hadith stating that a living human was hoisted physically into the sky.

• The Universal Law of Earth: Quran 7:25 explicitly decrees that all human beings live on earth, die on earth, and are resurrected from the earth.

• Allah Has No Spatial Coordinate: Allah is transcendent beyond physical space. Raising someone “to Himself” means spiritual elevation and proximity of the soul.

• Prophetic & Companion Precedent: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ supplicated for Rafa (Warfa’ni) daily, and the Companions used the exact term Rafa’ahu Ilayh for the death and soul of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Caliphs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does Rafa mean in Islam?

Rafa is an Arabic verb that means to raise or elevate. When Allah raises (Rafa’a) humans, He only raises their souls. Never their bodies. It refers to spiritual elevation, honor, and closeness to Allah.

Does Quran 4:158 state that Jesus was raised physically to heaven?

No. Quran 4:158 states Bal Rafa’ahullahu Ilayh (“Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself”). It does not say to heaven or to the sky. It directly refutes the Jewish claim that Jesus died an accursed death on the cross by affirming that Allah exalted his spiritual status and took his soul to Himself.

Does Allah have a physical location or direction in the sky?

No. Classical Islamic orthodoxy (Aqeedah) is unanimous that Allah is transcendent and not confined to any physical space, direction, or cosmic boundary. Therefore, being raised “to Allah” cannot denote physical travel upward into the sky.

Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray for Rafa?

Yes. In authentic Hadith (such as Sunan Ibn Majah 898), the Holy Prophet ﷺ prayed between the two prostrations: “Warfa’ni” (“and raise me”). This was a prayer for spiritual exaltation, not physical flight into outer space.

What does the sequence in Quran 3:55 (Mutawaffika wa Rafi’uka) prove?

Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55) explicitly places Mutawaffika (causing to die a natural death) before Rafi’uka (exalting in rank). This establishes that Isa (AS) completed his natural life, died, and then his soul was exalted to Allah.

Introduction

Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul.

It never means the taking of the body & soul.

This rule is established by the Holy Quran itself in Surah Az-Zumar:

اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا

“Allah takes away the souls of human beings at the time of their death; and of those that are not yet dead, during their sleep.”

[Quran 39:42]

When Allah takes a person, He takes their soul. This occurs either at death, or temporarily during sleep. It never means taking a living physical body up into the sky.

Whoever claims that Allah takes a human being physically with both body and soul carries the entire burden of proof. There is zero Quranic verse, zero Hadith, and zero Arabic lexicon that supports such a claim.

1. Tawaffa in the Holy Quran (25 Verses)

The word Tawaffa is used 25 times in the Holy Quran where Allah takes humans.

Every single time, without exception, it means the taking of the soul. It either refers to causing someone to die or taking their soul during sleep. It never once refers to lifting a physical human body into heaven.

There is zero verse in the Quran where Allah takes a human and it means taking their body. Whoever claims otherwise must produce a single verse.

• For a complete breakdown of all 25 verses, read: Tawaffa in Quran | 25 Verses.

2. Tawaffa in Hadith Literature

In the Hadith literature, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeatedly used the word Tawaffa.

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ used it to describe death, including his own eventual passing and the death of previous prophets. Throughout the thousands of Hadith compilations, there is zero Hadith where Allah does Tawaffa of a human and it means taking their physical body to the sky.

• For the primary Hadith narrations and analysis, read: How Tawaffa is used in Hadith Literature.

3. Tawaffa in Arabic Lexicons & Dictionaries

Classical Arabic lexicons are completely unanimous on this word.

In Lisān al-ʿArab, the most authoritative lexicon of the Arabic language, it states:

تَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ إِذَا قَبَضَ نَفْسَهُ

“Allah caused him to die [Tawaffāhu Allāh] when He took his soul.”

[Lisan al-Arab, vol. 14, p. 440]

Authorities such as Tāj al-ʿArūs, Kitāb al-ʿAyn, Al-Qāmūs al-Muḥīṭ, and Lane’s Arabic-English Lexicon all document this exact same rule: when Allah does the Tawaffa of a person, it means He caused them to die and took their soul.

There is zero Arabic lexicon in existence stating that when Allah takes a human, He takes their physical body.

• Read the full list of classical dictionary citations: Meaning of Tawaffa in Lexicons & Dictionaries.

4. The View of the Salaf (Tafsir al-Tabari)

Some non-Ahmadi Muslim clerics claim there is an Ijmāʿ (consensus) from the early generations that Isa (AS) was taken physically alive to heaven.

This claim is historically false. Imam Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari (d. 310 AH), one of the greatest scholars of the Salaf, documented early Islamic beliefs in his famous exegesis (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān). In his commentary on Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55), Tabari records four different views held by the early Muslims regarding Isa (AS).

Three out of those four views translate Tawaffa as the taking of the soul, not the taking of the physical body. Two of these views explicitly state that Isa (AS) died. There was never any consensus that he was raised physically with his body.

• Read the full historical evidence: Is there a consensus (Ijma’) that Isa (AS) is Alive?.

5. The Tafsir of Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari

The greatest commentator of the Holy Quran among the Companions was Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA).

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the most authentic book of Hadith after the Quran, Ibn Abbas (RA) gave the direct definition of Mutawaffika in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55):

قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: مُتَوَفِّيكَ: مُمِيتُكَ

“Ibn Abbas said: Mutawaffīka means: Mumītuka [I will cause you to die].”

[Sahih al-Bukhari, p. 745]

Imam Bukhari deliberately included this statement in his Sahih. If anyone claims this report is not Sahih, the burden of proof is entirely on them. There is consensus among Hadith scholars that narrations brought with definitive wording (Jazm) by Imam Bukhari in his Sahih are authentic, and authentic from the perspective of Imam Bukhari himself.

• Read more on the commentary of Ibn Abbas (RA): Ibn Abbas (RA) on the Death of Isa (AS).

• Learn why this narration is authentic: Muallaq Ahadith in Bukhari.

6. Can Tawaffa Mean Sleep?

Non-Ahmadis often ask: can Tawaffa mean sleep?

Yes, Tawaffa can mean sleep when night or sleep is explicitly mentioned in the context (such as in Surah Az-Zumar 39:42 and Surah Al-An’am 6:60).

However, even in sleep, what does Allah take? He takes the soul, never the body. During sleep, a person’s body remains on their bed on earth. Therefore, if someone argues that Isa (AS) was put to sleep in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:55), his physical body must have remained on this earth. Sleep does not fly a physical human body into outer space.

• Read the full explanation: Can Tawaffa mean sleep? Full Explanation | Quran 39:42.

7. Can Tawaffa Mean “Take Fully”?

Some opponents claim that Tawaffa means “to take fully,” arguing that Allah took Isa (AS) physically with his body and soul into heaven.

This claim is false. Whenever Allah takes a human being, He only takes the soul. It never means taking the physical body. Whoever claims that Allah takes the body carries the entire burden of proof to produce a single Quranic verse or Hadith.

• Read the detailed refutation: Can Tawaffa Mean “Take Fully”?.

• Understand active vs passive forms: Tawaffa vs Tuwaffa: Active and Passive Meaning in Arabic.

8. The 1,000 Rupee Challenge of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS)

In his book Izala-e-Auham (1891), Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) issued an open monetary challenge to the entire world.

He offered a prize of 1,000 Rupees to anyone who could produce a single example from the Holy Quran, the Hadith, or classical Arabic poetry where Allah takes a living human being using the verb Tawaffa, and it means taking their physical body.

Over 130 years have passed. Zero opponents have ever claimed the prize.

• Read the terms of the challenge: Claim of Mirza Ghulam (AS) Ahmad on Tawaffa.

Summary

• The Core Meaning: Tawaffa means to take something. When Allah takes a human, it only means taking the soul. It never means taking the body and soul.

• Zero Proof for Bodily Ascension: There is zero Quranic verse, zero Hadith, and zero Arabic lexicon where Allah takes a human and it means taking their body.

• The View of the Salaf: Early Muslim scholars documented by Imam al-Tabari held that Tawaffa means taking the soul. Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari explicitly defined it as death (Mumituka).

• The Sleep Argument: Even during sleep, only the soul is taken while the body remains on earth.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does Tawaffa mean in Islam?

Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul. It never means the taking of the body & soul.

How many times is Tawaffa used in the Quran for humans?

The word Tawaffa is used 25 times in the Holy Quran where Allah takes humans. Every single time, without exception, it means the taking of the soul (death or sleep). It never means taking the physical body.

Can Tawaffa mean sleep?

Yes, Tawaffa can mean sleep when sleep or night is explicitly stated in the context (as in Quran 39:42). But even in sleep, Allah takes only the soul while the physical body remains on earth.

Did Ibn Abbas (RA) explain the Tawaffa of Isa (AS)?

Yes. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) explicitly defined Mutawaffika in Quran 3:55 as Mumituka (“I will cause you to die”).

Is there any Hadith or Quranic verse where Tawaffa means taking the physical body?

No. There is zero Quranic verse and zero Hadith in all of Islamic literature where Allah does Tawaffa of a human and it means taking their physical body to heaven.
